hypotheses.title: Unified H29-HPVC + Walker Lane Anisotropic Seismic-Fabric Structure-Tensor Coherence (targeting the SE quadrant deficit)
layers: deq_n100a15 and ieq_n100a15 earthquake density rasters + geod_shearrate
H29-1 hydrothermal/piedmont/destriped-magnetic/Frangi-vesselness feature stack + weighted 300 m CELF cover
hypotheses.signature: Multi-scale structure-tensor anisotropy (lambda1 - lambda2)/(lambda1 + lambda2) of earthquake-density ridges (`ieq_n100a15`, `deq_n100a15`) aligned with dextral/transtensional `geod_shearrate` gradients in the Hawthorne/Tonopah Walker Lane belt, fused into the H29-S 2-stage vesselness + weighted CELF pipeline.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Active transtensional strands in the SE Mina deflection / Walker Lane rupture distributed stepover zones with strong microseismic lineament fabric despite discontinuous Holocene alluvial scarps.
hypotheses.confounders: Off-fault earthquake swarms, catalog-completeness gradients, and over-smoothed hypocenter kernels.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: H29-1 beat D0 in NW (+0.0022), NE_LidarGap (+0.0024), and SW (+0.0032), losing only SE (-0.0025) because H29-1 omitted D0's `ieq/deq` structure-tensor coherence. Combining H29-S with multi-scale seismic-fabric coherence has never been run.
hypotheses.data_gate: Existing hash-pinned raster bands; no new external download needed.
hypotheses.validation: Preregister on fresh unused seeds >= 270 against both D0 and H29-S before running.

hypotheses.title: Standalone Quality-Filtered Hydrothermal Upflow & Oblique Transfer-Zone Detector (H30-2 / H30-3)
hypotheses.signature: Station-deduplicated well/spring thermal excess (T - 20 C > 0, T <= 350 C), quartz/chalcedony/cation geothermometer excess (max T_geo - 50 C > 0), and oblique transfer-zone strike-rotation boundaries (|grad cos(2*theta_mag)| + |grad sin(2*theta_mag)|) weighted by geodetic shear rate.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Nearly 50% of Great Basin geothermal systems are blind (no surface fault rupture; Faulds & Hinz 2015) due to smectite/illite clay caps and young alluvial cover, and transverse transfer zones fracture into distributed small-offset shears omitted by scarp-focused aerial/LiDAR mapping.
hypotheses.confounders: Lateral down-hydraulic-gradient warm-water outflow plumes in permeable piedmont gravels; clustered agricultural/municipal well fields; pre-Cenozoic plutonic/thrust contacts.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Addendum D (H27-12) tested only Euclidean distance to well/spring coordinates regardless of temperature (+0.0005 PR-AUC, refuted). Incorporated as bands 5-7 of the promoted H30-1 stack; standalone ablation without up-dip potential-field advection remains untried.
hypotheses.data_gate: Hash-pinned gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv (27,092 rows) and raster bands already staged in data_cache/.
hypotheses.validation: Included inside promoted H30-1 (seeds 240-244, canary AUCs 0.5390, 0.5666, 0.5700); standalone ablation requires fresh seeds >= 270.
hypotheses.status: PARTIALLY TESTED INSIDE PROMOTED H30-1; standalone ablation untried.

hypotheses.title: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan Wave-Cut Paleo-Shoreline Contour-Parallelism Deconfounder
layers: Optional USGS 3DEP 1-m / 10-m absolute elevation (1,200-1,340 m Sehoo highstand belt)
hypotheses.signature: Measures sin^2(theta_scarp - theta_contour) to suppress non-tectonic horizontal wave-cut benches wrapping closed basin contours (~1,330-1,338 m) while retaining tectonic normal faults that cut obliquely across contours.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Eliminates the primary non-fault scarp false-positive mimic in Winnemucca/Fallon/Carson Sink sub-basins, freeing 300 m CELF budget for genuine piedmont faults.
hypotheses.confounders: Low-angle detachment toes locally sub-parallel to basin margin contours.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: No contour-parallelism shoreline filter has ever been tested in GEMSDOE27.
hypotheses.cost: medium; partial local via det_elev, full mask via public-domain USGS 3DEP tiles (`dem_links.json`)
hypotheses.data_gate: Local det_elev ready immediately; raw 3DEP elevation tiles require outbound access to USGS `prd-tnm` S3 (`https://data.usgs.gov/datacatalog/data/USGS:77ae0551-c61e-4979-aedd-d797abdcde0e`).

hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Rapidly aggrading bajadas erase continuous surface scarps within centuries while preserving aligned canyon-mouth knickpoints.
